title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Oxidizing Mn(II) linkers in a {P8W48} framework lowers Cu(II) uptake because the framework charge decreases and bound copper is released.
explanation: Photometric uptake experiments show native W2 taking up 0.73 mmol Cu(II) per gram versus 0.37 mmol g−1 for the oxidized W2ox phase in which Mn(II) has been converted to Mn(III). The review explicitly attributes the drop to the reduced negative charge of the oxidized framework.
scope: Mn-linked {P8W48} framework W2 and its oxidized form W2ox.
conditions: Cation-uptake tests over 24 h, compared for W2 and W2ox.
caveats: This charge-uptake relationship is reported for copper on this Mn framework, not as a quantified rule for every redox-active POM framework.
